title: Transitivity for completed naive cotangent complexes
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $B\to C$ be a homomorphism of commutative $A$-algebras, with $B,C$ complete for the ideals generated by $I$, and with $B/IB,C/IC$ finite type over $A/I$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Then $B,C$ are Noetherian. For $(E,F)=(A,B),(A,C),(B,C)$, let $I_E=IE$ and choose a finite restricted-polynomial presentation $\widehat{E[t_1,\ldots,t_m]}_{I_E}\twoheadrightarrow F$ with kernel $Q$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]; such presentations exist. Set $L_{F/E}^{\wedge}=(Q/Q^2\xrightarrow{\delta}F^{\oplus m})$ in degrees $-1,0$, with $\delta(\bar f)=(\partial f/\partial t_i\bmod Q)_i$ using the continuous extensions of polynomial derivatives. These complexes are independent of presentation up to homotopy, meaning chain maps in both directions with composites chain homotopic to the identities. Write $H^{-1}(L)=\ker\delta$ and $H^0(L)=\operatorname{coker}\delta$. There are $C$-linear maps, induced by the algebra homomorphisms and the connecting map, giving the exact sequence
$$H^{-1}(L_{B/A}^{\wedge}\otimes_B C)\longrightarrow H^{-1}(L_{C/A}^{\wedge})\longrightarrow H^{-1}(L_{C/B}^{\wedge})\longrightarrow C\otimes_B H^0(L_{B/A}^{\wedge})\longrightarrow H^0(L_{C/A}^{\wedge})\longrightarrow H^0(L_{C/B}^{\wedge})\longrightarrow0.$$
Here tensor products are ordinary module tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and the leftmost complex is obtained by tensoring the two displayed terms and the differential, without claiming that tensoring commutes with kernels. Exactness means that at each term with incoming and outgoing arrows the image of the incoming map equals the kernel of the outgoing map.

source.place: Tag 0ALM (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), the six-term completed transitivity sequence; Tag 0AJR (equation-NL) defines the complexes and Tag 0GAE (lemma-NL-up-to-homotopy) gives presentation independence. Tags 0AJP (lemma-topologically-finite-type) and 0AJQ (lemma-topologically-finite-type-Noetherian) supply presentations and Noetherianity.

proof.text: Choose $b_1,\ldots,b_r\in B$ lifting algebra generators of $B/IB$. Put $R=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ and $P=\widehat R_I$. The ideal $I$ is finitely generated by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], so [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] makes $P$ complete. Since $B$ is complete for $IB$, evaluation $x_i\mapsto b_i$ extends to a unique continuous $A$-algebra map $P\to B$ by [lem-per-completed-polynomial-taylor-evaluation]. This map is onto: given $b\in B$, choose $p_1\in R$ with $b-p_1(b_i)\in IB$. If $p_n$ has error in $I^nB$, express that error as a finite sum $\sum a_jc_j$ with $a_j\in I^n$, replace each $c_j$ modulo $IB$ by a polynomial $q_j(b_i)$, and set $p_{n+1}=p_n+\sum a_jq_j$. Then $p_{n+1}-p_n\in I^nR$ and the new error lies in $I^{n+1}B$. The compatible classes of $p_n$ define $p\in P$ whose image is $b$ by completeness and separatedness of $B$. With $J=\ker(P\to B)$ this gives $B=P/J$. The same construction gives a finite completed polynomial presentation of $C/A$.

source.place: Tag 0AJP (lemma-topologically-finite-type), last paragraph, with the successive-approximation proof of surjectivity written out

proof.text: The ring $R=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], $P$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], and $B=P/J$ is Noetherian by the same finite-type permanence theorem applied to the quotient. Similarly $C$ is Noetherian. In particular $J$ and all the other presentation ideals below are finitely generated. The same images of generators of $C/IC$ over $A/I$ generate it over $B/IB$: their $A/I$-polynomial expressions are also $B/IB$-polynomial expressions. Thus $C$ is complete for $IB$, and the construction of Step 1, with $B$ as base, gives $C=S/J'$ with $S=\widehat{B[y_1,\ldots,y_s]}_{IB}$. All three complexes in the statement are consequently defined.

For two presentations $F=P_1/Q_1=P_2/Q_2$ of the same algebra over a fixed base $E$, lift the images in $F$ of each variable of $P_1$ to elements $g_i\in P_2$. Restricted substitution gives a presentation map $\phi:P_1\to P_2$: its composite with $P_2\to F$ and the map $P_1\to F$ are evaluations at the same images of the variables, so they agree by the uniqueness of evaluation, and $\phi(Q_1)\subseteq Q_2$. On degree $-1$ send $[f]$ to $[\phi(f)]$; on degree $0$ send $\mathrm dx_i$ to $\sum_j(\partial_jg_i\bmod Q_2)\mathrm dy_j$. The first-order calculus node gives the chain rule, so these are a chain map. For another lift $g_i'$, define $h:F^{\oplus r}\to Q_2/Q_2^2$ by $h(\mathrm dx_i)=[g_i-g_i']$. Taylor modulo $Q_2^2$, applied in the complete Noetherian ring $P_2$ with $H=Q_2$, gives $\phi^{-1}-\phi'^{-1}=h\delta_1$ on $Q_1/Q_1^2$. Differentiating $g_i-g_i'$ gives $\phi^0-\phi'^0=\delta_2h$. Thus the chain maps are homotopic. Substitution respects composition and the identity, so choosing lifts in both directions gives composites homotopic to the identities. This proves the asserted homotopy independence. The same equations remain true after termwise tensoring with any algebra, since tensoring respects sums and compositions; no preservation of kernels is used.

source.place: Tag 0GAE (lemma-NL-up-to-homotopy), Steps 1 and 2; the diagonal homotopy is explicit

proof.text: Put $T=\widehat{A[x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s]}_I$ and $U=P[y_1,\ldots,y_s]$. Both $P$ and $U$ are Noetherian by finite-type permanence and completion Noetherianity. For every $n\geq1$, the completion-mod-ideal statement, applied to $R$ with $I^nR$, identifies $P/I^nP=R/I^nR$: the $I$- and $I^n$-completion limits agree by cofinality, since every positive integer is bounded by a multiple of $n$. Coefficientwise reduction therefore identifies $\widehat U_I=T$. Apply exactness of finite-module completion to $0\to JU\to U\to B[y]\to0$ over the Noetherian ring $U$. The outer two modules are finite over $U$, as is its ideal $JU$. This gives a surjection $q:T\twoheadrightarrow S$. By the finite-module tensor-completion comparison, the image of $(JU)^\wedge=T\otimes_U JU$ in $T$ is the ideal $JT$ generated by the images of $J$. Hence $\ker q=JT$. Put $K=q^{-1}(J')$. Then $T/K=C$ and $J'=K/JT$, with the variable images prescribed by the two original presentations.

source.place: Tag 0ALM (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), combining presentations; the quotient identification is expanded using Tags 00MA, 00MB and 05GG

proof.text: Define $a:(J/J^2)\otimes_B C\to K/K^2$ by $[j]\otimes c\mapsto c[j]$, and $b:K/K^2\to J'/(J')^2$ by $[k]\mapsto[q(k)]$. They are well-defined $C$-linear maps: $JT\subseteq K$, so products of two elements of $J$ die modulo $K^2$, and multiplication by a representative in $T$ depends only on its class in $C=T/K$. The map $b$ is onto because $q(K)=J'$. Since $(J')^2=(K^2+JT)/JT$, its kernel is $(JT+K^2)/K^2$. That is precisely the image of $a$: every element of $JT$ is a finite sum $\sum t_jj_j$, and its class is $\sum a([j_j]\otimes\bar t_j)$. Thus $(J/J^2)\otimes_B C\to K/K^2\to J'/(J')^2\to0$ is exact. There is no assertion that $a$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0ALM (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), lower row of the displayed diagram, exactness verified by ideal arithmetic

proof.text: Under the differential construction of [def-per-completed-polynomial-conormal], the degree-zero row is the split sequence $0\to C^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{u\mapsto(u,0)}C^{\oplus r}\oplus C^{\oplus s}\xrightarrow{(u,v)\mapsto v}C^{\oplus s}\to0$. The vertical maps from Step 5 to this row are respectively $\delta_{B/A}\otimes1_C$, $\delta_{C/A}$, and $\delta_{C/B}$. The squares commute: for $j\in J$, differentiation in an $x$ variable gives the same partial derivative in $P$ and $T$, while its $y$ derivatives are zero; for $k\in K$, reduction of its $y$ derivatives under $q$ is the $y$ derivative of $q(k)$ in $S$, since $q$ reduces the $x$ coefficients and fixes $y$. This last identity holds coordinatewise on polynomial reductions modulo $I^n$ and therefore on the completed derivatives. These calculations extend $C$-linearly to the two entire conormal modules.

source.place: Tag 0ALM (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), commutativity of the displayed diagram, using Tag 0AJR (equation-NL)

proof.text: Work in the abelian category of $C$-modules provided by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian]. The rows of Steps 5 and 6 meet exactly the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-snake-lemma-abelian]: the conormal row is right exact and the free row begins with a monomorphism and is exact. The snake lemma gives the exact sequence of the three vertical kernels followed by the three vertical cokernels. Its final arrow is onto because the last map of the free row is onto. Explicitly, the connecting map sends $z\in\ker\delta_{C/B}$ to the class of $v\in C^{\oplus r}$ for a lift $w\in K/K^2$ of $z$ with $\delta_{C/A}(w)=(v,0)$. Changing $w$ by $a(t)$ changes $v$ by $(\delta_{B/A}\otimes1)(t)$, so this is the prescribed connecting class. The three kernels are the displayed $H^{-1}$ terms; the last two cokernels are the displayed $H^0$ terms.

source.place: Tag 0ALM (lemma-exact-sequence-NL), final sentence, applying the snake lemma

proof.text: The remaining cokernel is canonically $C\otimes_B H^0(L_{B/A}^{\wedge})$. Indeed the maps $[v\otimes c]\mapsto c\otimes[v]$ and $c\otimes[v]\mapsto[v\otimes c]$ are inverse maps between $\operatorname{coker}(\delta_{B/A}\otimes1_C)$ and $C\otimes_B\operatorname{coker}\delta_{B/A}$; each is well-defined by the tensor relations and the relation $[\delta(j)]=0$. Replacing that cokernel in Step 7 yields exactly the asserted six-term sequence ending in zero. Step 3 identifies any other choices of the three presentation complexes by chain homotopies (also after ordinary tensoring), so the construction provides the asserted maps on the complexes chosen in the statement. In particular the first term is $\ker(\delta_{B/A}\otimes1_C)$, not a claim that tensoring preserves $\ker\delta_{B/A}$.
